title: Wave-based Launch Slate & Staging Owner Checklist (Runtime / Console / API)
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a reusable wave-based launch slate and a clear staging-owner checklist for coordinated launches that span Runtime, Console, and API surfaces. This ticket captures the planning artifacts, owner assignments, gating criteria, capacity reservations, and communication protocol for 2-3 week release trains where runtime changes have cross-surface impact (e.g., model rollout, KV cache changes, batching engine updates).

Scope: this playbook is for product and release leads to drive multi-surface launches that need synchronized staging windows across hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It focuses on wave definitions, staged owner responsibilities, observability/rollback gates, and a pre-cutover checklist that can be automated in the launch conductor.

Out of scope: deep runbook for infra toil, platform migration projects, or one-off emergency hotfixes. Those will continue to use the incident runbook flow.

Why now: recent runtime rollout (runtime-1.18) and a Console UX release were on separate cadences and caused two coordination gaps: 1) missing regional capacity reservations for canaries, and 2) ambiguous oncall ownership for partial rollbacks. This slate aims to remove those ambiguities and reduce launch friction and failure blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: A documented wave schema exists (Wave A: internal canary; Wave B: partner canary; Wave C: public) with clear timing and duration for each wave
A single staging-owner roster is published for each wave, listing primary and secondary owners for Runtime, Console, API, Infra, and SRE
Pre-cutover automation checks (smoke API, tail latency, error rate, cost delta) are codified and wired to the launch conductor dashboard
Capacity reservations and quota holds are confirmed for Dedicated pools and regional hosted capacity for the canary windows
Rollback and fallback steps are documented per surface, and a runbook link is present for any action that requires infra intervention
Communication templates (Slack channel naming, stakeholder pings, customer advisory copy) are created and validated with comms/PD
Post-launch evaluation template exists to capture quality regressions, cost delta, and any SLO breaches within 72 hours
milestones: 2026-03-05: Draft wave schema and owner roster (internal review)
2026-03-12: Validation with SRE and Infra for capacity reservations
2026-03-20: Integrate smoke checks into launch conductor (PR created)
2026-04-10: Final pre-cutover signoff and gating checklist complete
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive batching improvements reduce cost but increase tail-latency risk; we will gate batching changes behind latency SLOs and split into non-blocking background opt-in for a small % of traffic
We decided to reserve dedicated pool headroom for the partner canary rather than rely on best-effort burst so that partner SLAs are preserved
We will use the existing launch-conductor integration but add two new webhook checks for prefix-KV cache warmness and per-route cost delta
